Caro-Kann Defense.name: Caro-Kann Defense
Caro-Kann Defense.theme: Solid pawn structure and a healthy king, trading dynamic initiative for long-term endgame stability.
keyPlans: Develop the light-squared bishop outside the pawn chain to f5 or g4 before locking the structure with ...e6.
Execute the central break with ...c5 to challenge White's d4 pawn center.
In the Advance Variation (3. e5), immediately activate the bishop to Bf5, followed by ...e6 and ...c5.
In the Classical Variation (3. Nc3 dxe4 4. Nxe4 Bf5), swap knights if necessary and steer into an endgame where Black's pawn structure has zero weaknesses.
Caro-Kann Defense.criticalPieces: Light-squared bishop (Bf5/Bg4) — do not let it get trapped behind the e6-pawn.
Caro-Kann Defense.pitfalls: Avoid passive development where the f5 bishop is chased and traded without compensation or trapped by h4-g4 pawn storms.

Sicilian Defense.name: Sicilian Defense
Sicilian Defense.theme: Asymmetrical counter-attack fighting directly for central imbalance and queen-side counterplay.
keyPlans: Leverage the semi-open c-file with rooks on c8 and queen pressure on c7/a5.
Watch for White's f4-f5 or g4 kingside pawn storms; respond with timely central strikes (...d5 or ...e5).
Minor piece harmony: Knights coordinate on c6 and f6 (or d7), dark-squared bishop controls the diagonal from e7 or g7.
Exchange White's active knight on d4 if it limits Black's piece mobility.
Sicilian Defense.criticalPieces: Dark-squared bishop (e7 in Scheveningen/Najdorf, g7 in Dragon) defends the king and attacks the center.
Sicilian Defense.pitfalls: Greedy queen raids or delaying kingside castling while White rips open central files with d4 sacrifices.

French Defense.name: French Defense
French Defense.theme: Solid central wedge with fixed pawn chains; Black seeks to undermine White's pawn base on d4.
keyPlans: Assault White's pawn chain base with ...c5, followed by ...Nc6 and ...Qb6 to overload d4.
Solve the problem of the 'French Bishop' (light-squared bishop on c8) via ...b6 and ...Ba6, or ...Bd7 followed by ...Be8-g6.
In the Advance Variation (3. e5 c5 4. c3), hammer d4 relentlessly before preparing the second break with ...f6.
In the Winawer (3. Nc3 Bb4), pin the knight, damage White's queenside pawns with Bxc3+, and exploit the doubled c-pawns.
French Defense.criticalPieces: Light-squared bishop (c8) is naturally restricted; liberating it or trading it off via Ba6 is a high strategic priority.
French Defense.pitfalls: Suffocating from passive defense: failing to strike at c5 or f6 allows White a free attacking hand on the kingside.

Italian Game.name: Italian Game
Italian Game.theme: Classical central tension focusing on development and pressure on the sensitive f7/f2 weakness.
keyPlans: White aims to build a broad pawn center with c3 and d4, or play the Giuoco Pianissimo with d3 for slow positional pressure.
Black seeks harmonic development with ...Bc5, ...Nf6, and timely castling, preparing central counter-punches with ...d5.
Control the a2-g8 and a7-g1 diagonals with active light/dark-squared bishops.
In the Two Knights Defense (3...Nf6), Black sacrifices a pawn with 4. Ng5 d5 5. exd5 Na5 for massive development lead and piece activity.
Italian Game.criticalPieces: The Italian Bishop (c4 for White, c5 for Black) dictating diagonal pressure.
Italian Game.pitfalls: Neglecting king safety or leaving the f7/f2 square vulnerable to tactical pins like Bg5 or knight leaps to g5/d5.

Ruy Lopez.name: Ruy Lopez
Ruy Lopez.theme: The Spanish Torture: enduring strategic pressure on Black's e5 stronghold and kingside structure.
keyPlans: White maneuvers the b1 knight via d2-f1-g3 to assist kingside attacking prospects.
Black commonly pushes ...a6 and ...b5 to dislodge White's light-squared bishop, anchoring knights on c6/a5 and controlling c5.
In the Closed Ruy Lopez, White maintains central tension with c3 and d4 while Black prepares ...c5 or ...d5.
In the Berlin Defense (3...Nf6 4. O-O Nxe4), Black accepts the endgame double-pawn structure in exchange for the bishop pair and resilience.
Ruy Lopez.criticalPieces: White's light-squared bishop on c2/b3; preserve it at all costs from trades with Black's knight.
Ruy Lopez.pitfalls: Black allowing White full central domination without achieving the ...c5 counterbreak or conceding premature pawn weaknesses.

Queen's Gambit.name: Queen's Gambit
Queen's Gambit.theme: White sacrifices a wing pawn (c4) to establish total dominance over the center squares d4 and e4.
keyPlans: If accepted (2...dxc4), White regains the pawn with e3/e4 and Bxc4, controlling the center.
In Queen's Gambit Declined (2...e6), Black maintains the d5 anchor and focuses on resolving the c8 bishop via ...b6 or eventual ...c5.
In the Slav Defense (2...c6), Black supports d5 without blocking the c8 bishop, keeping options open for ...Bf5 or ...Bg4.
Minority Attack (in Carlsbad pawn structure): White pushes b4-b5 to create an isolated or backward pawn on c6 for Black.
Queen's Gambit.criticalPieces: Black's c8 bishop: locked behind e6 in the QGD, active outside in the Slav.
Queen's Gambit.pitfalls: Black attempting to stubbornly hold onto the c4 pawn in the QGA with ...b5, leading to queenside ruin.

King's Indian Defense.name: King's Indian Defense
King's Indian Defense.theme: Hypermodern battle: Black surrenders the center early to launch a vicious kingside pawn storm against White's monarch.
keyPlans: Establish the setup: 1...Nf6, 2...g6, 3...Bg7, 4...O-O, 5...d6, and strike the center with ...e5.
Once the center locks after d4-d5, Black reroutes the f6 knight to h5 or e8 and unleashes the ...f5-f4 pawn avalanche.
White attacks furiously on the queenside with c5 and b4, opening the c-file.
It is a race: White wins on the queenside if Black fails to deliver checkmate on the kingside.
King's Indian Defense.criticalPieces: King's Indian Bishop on g7: initially sleeping, becomes a laser beam across the long diagonal once center clarifies.
King's Indian Defense.pitfalls: Black hesitating on the kingside: playing timid positional moves while White crushes the queenside means swift defeat.

London System.name: London System
London System.theme: Universal, hyper-solid schematic setup for White based on rapid development and a rock-solid pyramid center.
keyPlans: Develop 1. d4, 2. Bf4, 3. e3, 4. Nf3, 5. c3, 6. Nbd2, 7. Bd3 before committing to action.
Anchor a knight on e5, supported by pawns on d4 and f4 (the Stonewall pivot).
If Black challenges the f4 bishop with ...Bd6, retreat to g3 so that an exchange opens the h-file for White's rook.
Black counterplay: Strike early with ...c5 and ...Qb6 targeting the weakened b2 square left by the departed f4 bishop.
pawnBreaks: e4 for White after piece preparation
London System.criticalPieces: White's dark-squared bishop on f4: the keystone of the system. Do not let it be traded unfavorably.
London System.pitfalls: Playing automatically: neglecting Black's tactical ideas like ...Qb6, ...cxd4, or ...Nh5 hunting the bishop.

Scandinavian Defense.name: Scandinavian Defense
Scandinavian Defense.theme: Immediate challenge to White's e4 pawn on move 1, opening lines at the cost of early queen moves.
keyPlans: In 2...Qxd5 3. Nc3 Qa5 (or Qd6/Qd8), Black secures a Caro-Kann-like pawn shell with ...c6 and ...e6.
Develop bishops outside the pawn chain (...Bf5 or ...Bg4) before closing with ...e6.
In the modern 2...Nf6, Black avoids early queen exposure and recaptures d5 with the knight or plays the Portuguese Gambit (...Bg4).
White looks to gain free tempos developing minor pieces (Nc3, d4, Nf3, Bc4/Bf4) and punish Black's queen maneuvers.
Scandinavian Defense.criticalPieces: Black Queen: ensure safe retreat squares (d8, c7, d6) and avoid getting trapped on a5.
Scandinavian Defense.pitfalls: Wasting moves saving the queen while falling fatally behind in development and king safety.

English Opening.name: English Opening
English Opening.theme: Flank opening exerting subtle, flexible control over the central d5 square without committing central pawns early.
keyPlans: Fianchetto the light-squared bishop to g2 to exert diagonal pressure toward the queenside.
Queenside expansion with a3, Rb1, and b4, coordinating with the g2 bishop.
If Black plays 1...e5 (Reversed Sicilian), White enjoys a Sicilian position with an extra tempo.
Transpositional flexibility: White can transpose into 1. d4 setups (Queen's Gambit, Catalan) whenever favorable.
English Opening.criticalPieces: White's g2 bishop: dominates the dark squares and pressures d5/c6/b7.
English Opening.pitfalls: Slow development allowing Black to seize total control of the center with ...e5, ...d5, and rapid piece coordination.

Nimzo-Indian Defense.name: Nimzo-Indian Defense
Nimzo-Indian Defense.theme: Hypermodern masterpiece: Black pins and trades for White's c3 knight, inflicting doubled pawns and taking rapid control of e4.
keyPlans: Pin the knight with ...Bb4 after 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 e6 3. Nc3 Bb4.
Inflict doubled pawns on White with ...Bxc3+ and systematically blockade the c4/c3 pawns.
Control the critical e4 outpost using a knight on f6 and pawn on d6 or f5.
White leverages the bishop pair to seek central expansion (e4) and attacking chances against Black's king.
Nimzo-Indian Defense.criticalPieces: Dark-squared bishop: Black gives it up on c3 to inflict structural damage, so Black must control dark squares with pawns.
Nimzo-Indian Defense.pitfalls: Black allowing White's bishop pair to open up the position with e4-d5 before Black secures the blockade.

General.name: Classical Principles
General.theme: Fundamental chess principles: rapid development, central control, king safety, and tactical awareness.
keyPlans: Control the four central squares (e4, d4, e5, d5) with pawns or active minor pieces.
Develop knights before bishops and do not move the same piece twice in the opening without concrete tactical reason.
Castle early (usually kingside) to safeguard your king and connect your rooks along central files.
Never leave pieces undefended ('loose pieces drop off'). Every piece must have a defender or a tactical justification.
pawnBreaks: Central pawn pushes that challenge the opponent's fortified squares.
General.criticalPieces: The King: prioritize shelter before initiating complications.
General.pitfalls: Premature queen raids, neglecting development to chase wing pawns, and leaving the king in the center.
